advice.claim: Recurring revenue from memberships provides predictable cash flow for the business.
advice.quote: Also recurring monthly revenue equals predictable cash flow.

advice.claim: Implementing memberships reduces the amount of time staff spend at the counter trying to resell one-time packages.
advice.quote: Let's reduce the time that our staff spend at the counter reselling packages.

advice.claim: Membership programs increase client retention and reduce the impact of competitors' advertising.
advice.quote: increasing client retention so this very much goes to the psychology of things again and if somebody feels like they are a belonging to you a member of yours they're much less likely to see your competitors advertising they actually take much less stock of that because they instantly go oh oh, I already have my membership.

advice.claim: Add value to high-end products by bundling or negotiating special volume deals with reps instead of offering discounts.
advice.quote: So maybe you can contact your rep and say, you know what, is there a product that you have available that I could maybe buy as a special deal if it's a volume buy? And maybe you can bundle something. thing. So that's a great way to add value versus discounting.

advice.claim: Use grandfathering to keep long-term clients on their existing plans while offering new pricing to new customers.
advice.quote: So what you might do, and one of the things that works well with memberships is grandfathering. Grandfathering pricing, grandfathering special things, and I always consider it like Fight Club. Nobody talks about Fight Club, but it's still there. So when I Oftentimes when I work with a salon and we move them over from what they're doing today to memberships, you know what? There's a client that's been coming in for 20 years and they always buy the same package and they always do the thing. Don't upset the apple cart. Let them keep doing that. But every new customer coming in gets this pricing and sees only this pricing.

advice.claim: Reward loyal members with small gifts or gift cards at specific milestones like six months or one year.
advice.quote: so maybe you reward somebody at the sixth month after their membership maybe it's something small maybe it's a you know a bottle of a tan extender but at a year let's work out how much that client spent with you because maybe throwing them a hundred dollar gift card wouldn't be a bad idea

advice.claim: Include membership offers in social media and email blasts, using a 'members-only' section to create FOMO.
advice.quote: if you don't have an e-blast or social posts currently, I want you to include memberships in those posts. If you have an e-blast, let's have a members-only section. Let's have people have FOMO, right? You want them to feel like they're missing out on something. Members only.

advice.claim: Use QR codes to encourage clients to leave reviews and share their experiences.
advice.quote: Throw up a QR code on your desk. See these right here? We're going to leverage you guys today. We want you to use this QR code and tell us how we're doing. and you should do the same with your clients

advice.claim: Offer limited-time or permanent membership upgrades during specific seasons.
advice.quote: Include seasonal upgrades, temporary upgrades available off peak. So I love this and I'm sure you guys do this at TAN Republic too. Do you offer people the chance to upgrade their membership? So let's say you have three tiers today or four tiers and you have a level two member, offer them as you get into to September, September to December, offer them a chance to a lifetime upgrade on their membership.

advice.claim: Offer membership upgrades during slow or off-peak seasons to maximize revenue.
advice.quote: offer upgrades during slow and off-peak seasons.

advice.claim: Provide perks like VIP status, gifts, or priority booking to recognize and reward top clients.
advice.quote: Recognize top clients with VIP perks, gifts, priority booking.

advice.claim: Use psychological pricing by keeping prices just under a round number (e.g., $99 instead of $100).
advice.quote: If you keep your pricing at $99 instead of $100, people will spend $99, but they don't want to spend $100.

advice.claim: Avoid long-term membership commitments and instead offer shorter terms like three months to make customers feel less confined.
advice.quote: we recommend that you do no longer than a three-month commitment

advice.claim: Offer a short commitment period for memberships to make clients feel less restricted.
advice.quote: we recommend that you do no longer than a three-month commitment

advice.claim: Focus on memberships because the volume of sales outweighs the loss from a few difficult clients.
advice.quote: you'll make way more on memberships then it's worth even talking about those couple of people who are jerks

advice.claim: Increase your prices if you haven't updated them recently to keep up with inflation and value.
advice.quote: I want you guys to look at your pricing. If you can do anything this year, look at your pricing and increase it.

advice.claim: Prioritize implementing a membership program before investing in high-end equipment like cocoons.
advice.quote: you only bring in a cocoon if you have memberships. If you don't have memberships, that's not your priority today. Your priority is to get memberships and then bring in a cocoon

advice.claim: Prioritize establishing a membership program before investing in high-end add-on equipment like cocoons.
advice.quote: you only bring in a cocoon if you have memberships. If you don't have memberships, that's not your priority today. Your priority is to get memberships and then bring in a cocoon

advice.claim: Use specialized equipment as a value-add to naturally upsell clients into higher-tier membership levels.
advice.quote: you utilize to upsell members, to upsell memberships, right? So now you have an all-access pass and you add the cocoon to it or a VIP or a platinum membership.

advice.claim: Find a service or feature you are passionate about to help drive more membership sales.
advice.quote: find something that you love and you've got passion for that helps you sell more memberships

advice.claim: Use your knowledge and the way you explain services to motivate customers to book.
advice.quote: it's the way you explain it and your knowledge to your customers that is really going to motivate them to do this

advice.claim: Use your knowledge of the products to motivate customers to book services.
advice.quote: it's the way you explain it and your knowledge to your customers that is really going to motivate them to do this

advice.claim: Explain the specific benefits of a product to the customer based on their specific skin concerns.

advice.claim: Tailor your sales pitch based on the specific profile of the customer you are speaking to.
advice.quote: But when I was talking to the clients, I would switch it up by who that person was.

advice.claim: Use specific selling points like speed and ease of use to overcome customer hesitation.

advice.claim: Do not be afraid to hire younger staff as they can be hardworking and are easy to train on work ethic.

advice.claim: Create a rewards program for staff based on behaviors that improve management operations, such as reliability and teamwork.

advice.claim: Include non-sales staff, such as bed cleaners, in the rewards program to ensure everyone feels valued.
advice.quote: you want to make sure that you're keeping it a little bit for everybody so that the bed cleaners can also get some rewards.

advice.claim: Reward staff for high-value actions like signing up members for EFTs or selling high-value products.

advice.claim: Distinguish between commission-based pay for sales performance and wage increases based on reliability and ease of management.
advice.quote: You make my life easier, right? You become not a problem. You're great to my clients. I don't have, you know, I don't have corrections or things to to fix with my clients and things like that. You teach my new staff well. That all makes my life

advice.claim: Base wages should be tied to how much the employee simplifies the owner's job and manages clients effectively, while commissions should be based on sales performance.

advice.claim: Offer non-monetary rewards and bonuses to staff, as this generation of workers often values these incentives more than just a higher paycheck.
advice.quote: But beyond any money that you give your staff, this new generation, more than money, they, believe it or not, their rewards and their bonuses and things like that mean more to them than money does.

advice.claim: Build a sense of community among your staff to improve retention and culture.
advice.quote: But what I have also found with this new generation, which has been really awesome, is, and I love it, is putting them together as a community.

advice.claim: Having staff stay overnight during a team-building event ensures they remain focused on the company and away from social distractions.
advice.quote: But truly it is the best way to get them completely all yours. If you don't stay the night, night you will lose the girls to, um, whatever their social is.

advice.claim: Providing words of affirmation is often more valuable to the current generation of workers than monetary compensation.
advice.quote: because the check in and words of affirmation, if I'm gonna, that's what I started with, words of affirmation for this generation actually means more to them than money every single time.

advice.claim: Use a timesheet and scheduling app like Homebase to manage staff hours and scheduling efficiently.

advice.claim: Use an automated scheduling app to send shift reminders to employees and manage time-off requests and shift trades.

advice.claim: Use digital checklists to track salon cleaning tasks and accountability.
advice.quote: So you can have your checklists in the same app and have them check off who did what.

advice.claim: Restrict clock-in windows to prevent employees from clocking in early before their shifts.

advice.claim: Use a payroll integration app to automate the process of importing timesheets and paying employees to eliminate manual double-checking.

advice.claim: Use software settings to restrict the window in which employees can clock in to prevent time theft.
advice.quote: you can restrict, because i know some salon owners are like well they're going to clock in early they're going to clock in this you can restrict when they can clock in it can be five minutes before their shift or two minutes before their shift so that you can actually stop the time stealing as they call it from the employees that are clocking in early before their shift and you haven't noticed it

advice.claim: Use a remote desktop application to monitor sales stats and manage salon operations from a remote location.

advice.claim: Utilize social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok as a primary tool for reaching customers and driving sales.

advice.claim: Use social media to reach customers and build your brand's image.

advice.claim: Create a loyalty program that rewards current customers for referring friends or family.

advice.claim: Use social media engagement tactics like 'tag a friend' to increase reach and visibility.

advice.claim: Create social media posts that encourage users to share, repost, and tag friends to increase your reach.
advice.quote: make it a post where they have to share it, repost it, tag a friend.

advice.claim: Respond to Google reviews to improve your ranking in search algorithms.

advice.claim: Maintain a clean and welcoming salon environment to build customer loyalty and facilitate sales.

advice.claim: Ensure your brand is recognizable and cohesive across all platforms by using consistent logos, fonts, colors, and verbiage.
